# EightyOne: full documentation

Every guide and reference page of https://docs.eightyone.app, concatenated. Generated: don't edit by hand.

<!-- https://docs.eightyone.app/guides/index.md -->

# EightyOne developer docs

EightyOne runs factories and field-service companies. Everything that happens there is a task: machines, work orders, stock, quality, maintenance. These docs are for people and AI agents who build on it: system integrators who set up and run client factories, and teams who connect their own systems.

## Ways in

| | For | Start with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **REST API** (`/api/v1`) | Integrations, scripts, ERP and MES connectors | [Getting started](getting-started.md), then the [API reference](../reference/capabilities.md) |
| **MCP server** (`/mcp`) | AI agents: Claude, Cursor, any MCP client | [Agents and MCP](agents-and-mcp.md) |
| **The `eightyone` skill** | Agents that set up or run a factory | [Agents and MCP](agents-and-mcp.md#the-skill) |
| **Webhooks** | Being told when something happens | [Webhooks](webhooks.md), then the [event reference](../reference/events.md) |
| **External ids** | Connectors that map their own ids to EightyOne records | [Integrations](integrations.md) |
| **Accounting** | QuickBooks and other books: customers, products, estimates, invoices, purchase orders | [Accounting](accounting.md) |
| **Factory specs** | Setting up a whole company from one file | [Commissioning](commissioning.md) |

The REST API and the MCP server are generated from one registry of capabilities. The same operation has the same name, input, rules and permissions on both, and both are logged the same way.

## Concepts

- [Tasks: everything is a task](tasks.md)
- [Production: work orders, routings, counts, lots](production.md)
- [Inventory: storage, bins, moves, counts](inventory.md)
- [Quality, maintenance and downtime](quality-and-maintenance.md)
- [Factory or managed services](factory-and-managed-services.md)

## Reference (generated)

- [Capabilities](../reference/capabilities.md): every operation, with its input, output, permission and REST path
- [OpenAPI 3.1](../reference/openapi.json): the REST API and its webhooks, machine-readable
- [Webhook events](../reference/events.md)
- [Errors](../reference/errors.md)
- [Permissions](../reference/permissions.md)
- [Factory spec schema](../reference/factory-spec.schema.json)
- [MCP tools](../skill/eightyone/reference/tools.md)

## Two rules that shape everything

- **No financial data.** EightyOne holds no prices, costs or rates: quantities and hours only. Integrations with accounting systems exchange ids, products and quantities.
- **An agent or a key acts as a person.** It has that person's permissions in one company, it is logged as them, and it can never do more than they could in the dashboard.

---

<!-- https://docs.eightyone.app/guides/getting-started.md -->

# Getting started

## Accounts and companies

- **One company is one tenant:** a factory or a managed-services business, with its own people, machines, stock and settings.
- **Companies are created by EightyOne staff only.** To get one for a client, ask EightyOne.
- A person can belong to several companies, with different permissions in each.

## Credentials

| | Use it for | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **API key** | Integrations and headless agents | A signed-in user creates it under **Platform → API → Keys**. It acts as that user, in one company, and can be narrowed to fewer permissions than the user has. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. |
| **OAuth sign-in** | Interactive agents (Claude, Cursor) | The MCP client opens an EightyOne sign-in page; the user approves. |
| **Service account** | Integrations that shouldn't act as a named person | A non-human user in a permission group (**Platform → API → Service accounts**), with its own keys. |

EightyOne stores no copy of your keys: they're issued and checked by EightyOne's identity provider. A key shows once, when it's created. A revoked key stops working at once.

## Your first call

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $EIGHTYONE_KEY" https://api.eightyone.app/api/v1/me
```

`me` returns the company the key acts in, the user, and their permissions. Every other call is scoped to that company: you never pass a company id.

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $EIGHTYONE_KEY" "https://api.eightyone.app/api/v1/tasks?limit=20"
```

## Conventions

- **Ids** are external ids: short strings such as `rpbVkyAl`. Products are addressed by SKU. Database numbers never appear in the API, except where a resource has no other id (reason codes, downtime events, purchase order lines). Each capability's reference says which.
- **Paged lists** take `limit` and `offset` and return `{ data, pagination: { limit, offset, total, hasMore } }`.
- **Errors** are [problem details](../reference/errors.md). Branch on `code`.
- **Retries:** send an `Idempotency-Key` header on writes. A retry with the same key and body returns the first answer, for 24 hours.
- **Dry runs:** `Prefer: dry-run` (REST) or `dryRun: true` (MCP) previews a write. It answers what would change and what it would set off, and changes nothing. Every write an agent can call can be previewed.
- **Rate limits** answer `429` with `rate_limited`. Back off and retry.
- **Tracing:** send `X-EightyOne-Transaction-ID` to tie your logs to ours. Each response carries one either way.

## Logging and audit

Every write is recorded under the person the key or agent acts as, in the company's **Audit Logs**. EightyOne also keeps a call log of every API and MCP call: who, which capability, the result and the duration. For writes, it also keeps the input (secrets redacted) for 90 days.

---

<!-- https://docs.eightyone.app/guides/agents-and-mcp.md -->

# Agents and MCP

EightyOne runs an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server. Any MCP client, such as Claude, Cursor or your own agent, can read a company's data and work in it, as the person who connected it.

## Connecting

- **URL:** `https://api.eightyone.app/mcp`. One connection is one company: if the person belongs to several, add `?company=<short name>`.
- **Sign in (OAuth):** interactive clients add the URL as a custom connector. EightyOne's sign-in page opens, and the person approves.
- **API key:** headless agents send a key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` ([Getting started](getting-started.md#credentials)).

Start with `me_get`: it shows the company, the person and their permissions. Tools the person can't use aren't listed.

## What an agent can do

- **Read:** tasks, machines and their status, work orders, downtime, analytics, storylines (a machine's or an order's history), inventory, quality, partner handoffs.
- **Set up a company:** `config_export`, `config_validate`, `config_plan`, `config_apply` ([Commissioning](commissioning.md)).
- **Run the floor:**
  - release work orders, and move, assign and complete tasks, filling in their forms;
  - record production counts;
  - open NCRs and disposition them;
  - report and classify machine stops, and enter meter readings;
  - move, receive, ship and count stock;
  - send work to partner companies.

The [tool list](../skill/eightyone/reference/tools.md) has the details. Anything not listed as a tool can still be reached with `capabilities_search` and `capabilities_call`.

## The rules agents work under

- **Preview, then confirm.** Every write an agent can call takes `dryRun: true`. The answer says whether the change would be accepted, what it changes, and what it sets off (stock posted, tasks created, notifications). The skill tells agents to show that to the person and wait for their OK before the real call.
- **Never destructive.** Deleting anything, cancelling a work order, withdrawing a handoff and pruning a factory spec are not available over MCP. An agent tells the person where to do them.
- **People give what only people can give:**
  - photos, signatures and scans are filled in in the app;
  - stop reasons, dispositions and count decisions come from a person, never from the agent's guess.
- **Company guidance.** Administrators can tell every agent working in their company something (**Settings → AI guidance**), and agents read it with `guide_get` topic `company`.

## The skill

The `eightyone` skill teaches an agent the domain and the jobs: commissioning a factory from a template, modelling a production line, configuring task types and forms, and running a shift. It's an [Agent Skill](https://agentskills.io): a `SKILL.md` with playbooks, a factory template and the generated tool reference.

- **Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add eightyone-app/eightyone`, then `/plugin install eightyone@eightyone`. The plugin also connects the MCP server.
- **Claude apps and other agents:** download `eightyone-skill-<version>.zip` from [Downloads](downloads.md) and upload it as a custom skill.

The skill is versioned with the API: each release's tool reference matches the server it was published from.

---

<!-- https://docs.eightyone.app/guides/tasks.md -->

# Tasks: everything is a task

In EightyOne, every piece of work is a **task**: a work-order operation, a repair, a preventive service, an inspection, an NCR, a stock move, a count, an approval, a request to a partner. What kind of task it is comes from its **task type**.

## Task types

A task type defines a kind of work:

- **Its form:** the fields people fill in, ordered. Field types include text, number (with target and limits), checkbox, select, date and time, photo, signature, location, barcode scan, products, storage and machine status. A field can be **required**, and it can be shown only when another field has a given answer.
- **Its rules:**
  - **SLAs:** the due time per priority.
  - **Gates:** what must be true to enter a status, such as fields filled in, a signature, or a member of certain groups.
  - **Failure coding:** a problem, a cause and a remedy, required before completion on maintenance types.
  - **Production:** the product it makes, standard setup and run minutes, the work center and the parameter set.
  - **Who:** a team, a required skill and a minimum rank.
- **Automation:**
  - the machine status it sets when a task opens or completes;
  - **flows** (when a task of this type reaches a status, create a task of another type);
  - recurrence (time-based preventive maintenance).

## Statuses

`open` → `preparation` → `ready` → `dispatched` → `submitted` (when the type is reviewed) → `done`.

- **`incomplete`:** not finished, with a reason. It can create a follow-up task for the rest.
- **`declined`:** refused, with a reason.

Status changes follow the rules people get in the dashboard and the app:
- a blocked task can't move on;
- changing a status needs **Change task status from mobile**, though people can always complete their own tasks;
- reassigning needs **Reassign tasks**.

## Forms and completion

Completing a task is filling in its form and setting it to done. Through the API or an agent, that's `tasks.submit_form` with the answers and the status (`tasks.get_form` lists the fields first).

- **Required fields** must be filled. The server checks every completed form, from any client.
- **Measurements outside their limits** fail the check. The completed task then opens an NCR of the company's NCR type, linked to it.
- **Machine-status fields** set the machine's status.
- **Inventory tasks** post their stock moves.
- **Producing tasks** post their output and consume their recipe.
- **Photos, signatures and scans** are given by people in the app. A task that requires one waits for them.

## Connections

Tasks link to each other:

- **dependency:** the second task waits for the first. It can't progress until the first is done, and goes back to open if it was already ready or dispatched.
- **follow:** the second follows the first (follow-ups use this).
- **created from:** the second was made from the first (NCRs from a failed check, kitting from a task with products, rework from a disposition).

`tasks.create` takes `after: { taskId, type }` to create a task already linked.

## Who sees what

Members see their own tasks. Seeing every task needs **See all tasks**, and team members see their teams' work. The API and agents see exactly what the person they act as sees.

---

<!-- https://docs.eightyone.app/guides/production.md -->

# Production: work orders, routings, counts, lots

## The model

- **Products** have an item class (raw, wip, finished, operations, spare part), a unit, and a tracking mode: none, lot, or serial. A product is either **bought** (it has vendors) or **made** (it has a **recipe**: the components one unit consumes, in whole units).
- **Work centers** group machines that can run the same operations.
- **Task types** are the operations: cut, form, weld, inspect. Each has its standard setup and run minutes, the work center it runs in, its parameter set (machine settings, versioned) and its form.
- **Routings** list the steps a product goes through, each a task type. A step can be a **gate**: the steps after it wait until it's done. Changing a routing creates a new version; released orders keep the version they started with.
- **Work orders** ask for a quantity of a product. Status: `draft` → `released` → `in progress` → `completed` → `closed` (or `cancelled`).

## Release

Releasing a work order (`work_orders.release`, which needs **Release work orders**) creates one operation task per routing step:

- on the step's machine, when its work center has exactly one;
- with the parameter set's released version pinned;
- each step after a gate waiting on it, through a dependency.

Its preview lists each operation it would create. Work orders usually come from an ERP: `work_orders.upsert` and `work_orders.batch_upsert` create and update draft orders by your system's id.

## Counts

- **During a run,** `tasks.record_counts` adds good and scrap quantities. Counts add up and feed OEE.
- **At completion,** a producing task needs its counts. They come either with the completion or from the counts recorded during the run.
- **Completing posts the output:**
  - the good quantity goes into stock;
  - the recipe is consumed (backflushed) from the order's kit cart, then the machine's line-side storage, then any goods bin, earliest lot expiry first.
- A work order completes by itself when its last operation is done.

## Lots and genealogy

- Receiving a lot-tracked product records its lot.
- Completing a work order for a lot-tracked product creates the produced lot.
- Consumption links one to the other, so a finished lot traces back to its supplier lots.
- Blocked and quarantined lots are never consumed or shipped.

## Downtime and OEE

Machines report stops from telemetry, or people report them. Stops are classified with reason codes. `analytics.oee`, `analytics.downtime` and `downtime_events.summary` turn counts, stops and standard times into availability, performance and quality.

---

<!-- https://docs.eightyone.app/guides/inventory.md -->

# Inventory: storage, bins, moves, counts

## Where stock is

- **Storage sites** hold **storage units** (a shelf, a rack, a bay, a van).
- Whose a site is decides what happens to the stock in it:
  - a company warehouse or a floor's storage: the company's own;
  - a client's site;
  - a technician's;
  - a customer's consigned stock, which can only ship back to that customer;
  - a partner company's custody.
- Every machine (SSU) has its own unit too.
- Stock sits in a unit **in a bin:**
  - **goods** (usable);
  - **bads** (damaged or scrapped);
  - **quarantine** (waiting for inspection);
  - **installed** (fitted into a machine);
  - **transit** (on the way).
- Only goods count as available.
- A **line item** is one product in one unit, in one bin, of one lot (or one serial).
- `storage_units.get` shows what a unit holds; `inventory.stock_levels` gives goods on hand per product and site.

## Moving stock

| | Capability | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move between units or bins | `stock.transfer` | Never more than the line holds. Name the lot or serial when the product is tracked. |
| Receive a delivery | `purchase_orders.receive` | Per PO line, into a unit. A lot-tracked product needs its lot. An inspection plan for the product or vendor quarantines the receipt and opens an inspection task. Never more than was ordered. |
| Ship to a customer | `shipments.create`, then `shipments.ship` | A draft holds no stock. Shipping takes goods out, checking the lot, the stock and consignment. A customer that's an EightyOne company receives them in its transit. Factories only. |
| Partner goods | `partner_deliveries.receive` | Goods a partner company sent you. |

Inventory tasks (moves done in the app) post the same way when completed. Purchase orders are quantities only: EightyOne holds no prices.

## Cycle counts

1. `inventory_counts.create`: a count of one unit. It snapshots what's expected, and creates the count task for operators when the company has an inventory task type.
2. Counts come from that task in the app, or from `inventory_counts.record_lines`.
3. `inventory_counts.finalize` freezes the expected quantities as they are now, works out each difference, and adds anything on hand the count never saw (counted 0). It flags lines whose stock moved while the count was open.
4. `inventory_counts.reconcile` posts the decisions, which needs **Adjust inventory**:
   - **accepted:** stock becomes the counted quantity;
   - **adjusted:** stock becomes a corrected quantity;
   - **ignored:** stock stays as it is.

   Every write-off needs an adjustment reason. The preview lists each addition, write-off and bin move.

## Reordering

A stock policy per product (and optionally per site) sets a minimum, or a reorder point. The reorder point is computed from lead time × measured consumption. When stock falls to it, `stock.reorder_triggered` fires once, and the product appears in `inventory.reorder_suggestions`. It re-arms when stock recovers.

---

<!-- https://docs.eightyone.app/guides/quality-and-maintenance.md -->

# Quality, maintenance and downtime

## Quality

- **Inspections** are tasks of inspection types. They're created:
  - by a routing step;
  - by an inspection plan on receiving (the receipt is quarantined until the inspection passes);
  - by people.
- **In-line checks:** a number field with limits (`lsl`, `usl`) is a measurement. A completed task with a measurement outside its limits opens an **NCR** of the company's NCR type, linked to it and carrying its machine and work order.
- **NCRs** are tasks too:
  - `ncrs.open` raises one from the task where a problem was found, with the affected lot or product;
  - `ncrs.disposition` records the decision, once per NCR, and needs **Disposition NCRs**.
- **Dispositions:**
  - **use as is:** recorded only;
  - **rework:** creates a rework task;
  - **scrap:** moves the quantity of the lot to the bads bin and blocks the lot;
  - **return:** blocks the lot for return to the vendor.

## Maintenance

- **Corrective work** is a task of a maintenance type, opened by a person, an issue report (from the app or a QR code), or a condition rule on machine data.
- **Failure coding:** maintenance types can require a problem, a cause and a remedy code to complete (`tasks.update` or `tasks.submit_form` with `problemCodeId`, `causeCodeId`, `remedyCodeId`). `analytics.failure_pareto` ranks failure modes.
- **Preventive maintenance** has three triggers:
  - **time-based:** a task type's recurrence schedules the next task when one completes;
  - **usage-based:** a meter (run hours, strokes, cycles) with a rule "every N" opens a task each time the meter advances by N;
  - **condition-based:** a rule on a live signal (temperature above 80) opens a task when it's crossed.
- **Meters:** manual meters take readings (`meters.record_reading`, the running total), and signal meters count from machine data. A reading's preview says which preventive tasks it would open.
- **Spare parts:** each machine lists its spare parts.

## Downtime

- **A stop** is one downtime event: when the machine stopped, when it ran again, and the reason it was given.
  - Machines with telemetry report their stops themselves (`auto`).
  - For others, people report them (`downtime_events.open` and `.close`).
- **Classifying** a stop (`downtime_events.classify`) gives it a downtime reason code. Agents classify only with the reason a person gives: an unclassified stop is a gap to report, not a guess to fill.
- **Analysis:**
  - `downtime_events.summary` gives stopped time per machine and reason;
  - `analytics.downtime` measures time spent in a DOWN or MAINTENANCE status;
  - `analytics.reliability` gives MTBF and MTTR.

---

<!-- https://docs.eightyone.app/guides/factory-and-managed-services.md -->

# Factory or managed services

A company is one of two kinds. Its kind decides what clients, sites and shipping mean.

| | Factory | Managed services |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clients | One: the company itself | Many: the customers it serves |
| Sites | Its floors and areas | Its clients' locations |
| SSUs | Its machines, lines and cells | The assets it maintains at clients' sites |
| Stock leaves by | Shipping to **customers** (off-system, or other EightyOne companies) | Being moved to client sites (installed), never shipped |
| Typical work | Work orders, operations, counts, quality, maintenance | Service and maintenance visits, installs |

Both use the same tasks, task types, forms, storage and analytics. Shipments, customers and consigned stock exist only in factories.

## Partners

Two EightyOne companies can work together:

- **Handoffs:** send a task to a partner; they get their own copy, and its status flows back.
- **Partner deliveries:** goods travel with a handoff, or with a shipment to a customer that is an EightyOne company. They arrive in the partner's transit and are received there.
- **Data requests:** ask a partner for data (for example, a production record), which they release as a data package.

Each company keeps its own data. A partner sees only what was sent to it.

---

<!-- https://docs.eightyone.app/guides/commissioning.md -->

# Commissioning: a company from one file

A **factory spec** is a company's whole setup as one JSON document: plant, supply, work, machine data, quality and people.

- Everything in it refers to everything else **by name**, so a spec from one company applies to another.
- A section you leave out isn't touched.

## The sections

| Stage | Sections |
| --- | --- |
| Plant | `ssuStatuses`, `reasonCodes`, `workCenters`, `sites` (with their storage and the SSU tree), `warehouses`, `settings` |
| Supply | `productCategories`, `vendors`, `products` (by SKU, with vendors, recipe and stock policies) |
| Organisation | `permissionGroups`, `roles`, `teams`, `skills` |
| Work | `parameterSets`, `taskTypes` (forms, SLAs, gates, flags), `routings` |
| Machines and quality | `machineData` (signals, meters, condition rules, spare parts), `flows`, `issues`, `inspectionPlans`, `guidance` |
| People | `people`: existing users only, with their roles, teams and skills |

The [schema](../reference/factory-spec.schema.json) has every field.

## The calls

1. **`config.export`:** the company's setup as a spec. It's the best example of the format, and the starting point for a change.
2. **`config.validate`:** problems, each with its path in the file (a status that doesn't exist, a gate naming a field the form lacks).
3. **`config.plan`:** what applying would do, item by item: creates, updates field by field, what's blocked by permissions, and what's in the company but not in the spec (left alone).
4. **`config.apply`:** applies the plan through the same rules as the dashboard, audited. If a change fails, the earlier ones stay and the answer names the failure. Fix the file and apply again: unchanged items are skipped.

Over REST, `prune` also removes what's in the company but not in the spec. Agents can't prune.

## Working as an SI

- **With an agent:**
  - the SI describes the factory or hands over documents;
  - the agent, with the `eightyone` skill, starts from a template, builds the spec, and shows the plan;
  - it applies after the SI's go-ahead, in stages for a large factory.
- **With files:**
  1. commission one reference factory;
  2. export it, and keep the spec in your own repository as your template;
  3. for each client, rename what's specific, validate, plan and apply.

  The skill's Brazos Metalworks template, a sheet-metal fabricator, was made that way.

## What a spec doesn't do

- **People:** a spec never invites anyone. Invite them in the dashboard; a spec can then give them roles, teams and skills.
- **Permissions:** nobody can grant more than they have themselves, and the company always keeps an administrator.
- **Versions:** changing a routing or a parameter set releases a new version, and orders already released keep theirs.
- **Companies:** only EightyOne staff create them.
- **Prices:** none, anywhere.

---

<!-- https://docs.eightyone.app/guides/webhooks.md -->

# Webhooks

**What it is:** EightyOne tells your systems when something happens, such as a task changing status, a work order released, a machine stopping or a lot created. It does this by sending an HTTPS `POST` to a URL you choose. Each message is signed, so your system can check it really came from EightyOne.

**Where:** in the dashboard, **Platform → API → Webhooks**, or the API's `webhooks.*` capabilities. You need **Manage webhooks** to create or change one.

## Setting one up

1. **New webhook:** give it a name, your HTTPS endpoint, and the events it should receive. Private and internal addresses are refused.
2. **Send test:** sends a signed `webhook.test` message to that endpoint only, so you can check your receiver.
3. **Recent deliveries:** each webhook lists what it sent, with the result. Filter by event type or status to find a failure.

A delivery your endpoint doesn't answer with a 2xx is retried after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 24 hours. Then it's marked failed, and the webhook counts the failure.

## What a delivery looks like

Messages follow the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/) format:

```
POST /your/endpoint
webhook-id: msg_2b9f…
webhook-timestamp: 1760860800
webhook-signature: v1a,<base64 signature>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "type": "task.status_changed", "timestamp": "2026-10-19T08:00:00.000Z", "data": { … } }
```

- **`type`** is the event; **`data`** is its content.
- Ids in `data` are the same ones the API uses: task and machine external ids, SKUs, work order ids. They are never internal database numbers.
- **`webhook-id`** stays the same on every retry of a message. Use it to ignore a message you've already handled.
- Messages can arrive out of order. Use `timestamp`, or fetch the current state from the API, when order matters.

The [event reference](../reference/events.md) lists every event and its fields; the [OpenAPI document](../reference/openapi.json) has them too, in its `webhooks` section.

## Checking a signature

EightyOne signs every message with its own key (Ed25519). There is **no secret** to copy or store: you verify with EightyOne's **public key**.
- The public key is shown on each webhook.
- Your system can fetch it from `https://api.eightyone.app/api/v1/webhook-signing-keys`. That URL needs no login.

To check a message:
1. Join `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and the raw request body with dots: `<id>.<timestamp>.<body>`.
2. The `webhook-signature` header holds one or more `v1a,<signature>` entries. Accept the message if any of them verifies against any published key.
3. Refuse a timestamp older than a few minutes, so an old message can't be replayed.

In Node.js:

```js
import { createPublicKey, verify } from "node:crypto";

// Fetch once and cache. During a key change two keys are listed, and both sign.
const response = await fetch("https://api.eightyone.app/api/v1/webhook-signing-keys");
const keys = (await response.json()).keys.map((k) =>
    createPublicKey({
        // An Ed25519 public key in the SPKI format Node expects: a fixed prefix plus the 32 key bytes.
        key: Buffer.concat([Buffer.from("302a300506032b6570032100", "hex"), Buffer.from(k.publicKey.slice(5), "base64")]),
        format: "der",
        type: "spki",
    }),
);

export function isFromEightyOne(headers, rawBody) {
    const id = headers["webhook-id"];
    const timestamp = Number(headers["webhook-timestamp"]);
    if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - timestamp) > 300) return false; // older than 5 minutes
    const signed = Buffer.from(`${id}.${timestamp}.${rawBody}`);
    return headers["webhook-signature"].split(" ").some((entry) => {
        const [version, signature] = entry.split(",");
        return version === "v1a" && keys.some((key) => verify(null, signed, key, Buffer.from(signature, "base64")));
    });
}
```

Verify the **raw** body, exactly as received. Parsing it and serializing it again changes the bytes, and the signature won't match.

## What changed (October 2026)

Webhooks moved to Standard Webhooks. If you built a receiver before, update it:

- **Signature:** `X-EightyOne-Signature` (HMAC with a per-webhook secret) is replaced by `webhook-signature`, verified with EightyOne's public key. Existing webhook secrets were removed, and none are issued any more.
- **Body:** `{ event, eventId, createdAt, data }` is now `{ type, timestamp, data }`. `eventId` is now the `webhook-id` header.
- **Content:** events carry the API's ids. For example, `task.created` has `task.id` (the external id) and `task.type: { id, name }`, instead of database ids such as `typeId`.
- **Reliability:** a message is recorded with the change that caused it. A change that's undone sends nothing, and a message is never lost when EightyOne restarts.

---

<!-- https://docs.eightyone.app/guides/integrations.md -->

# Integrations: mapping your ids

**What it is:** when you connect another system (an ERP, an MES, an accounting package) to EightyOne, the same customer, product or order has an id on each side. EightyOne can keep that mapping for you: you link your id to an EightyOne record once, then find either side from the other. Your connector then doesn't need a mapping table of its own.

**Where:** the API's `external_refs.*` capabilities ([reference](../reference/capabilities.md#external-refs)). Looking an id up needs **View company settings & integrations**. Linking and unlinking needs **Manage company settings & integrations**. Agents can look ids up over MCP, but linking is REST-only.

## A link

```json
{
    "system": "acme-erp",
    "externalType": "item",
    "externalId": "ITEM-77",
    "entityType": "product",
    "entityId": "SKU-1001"
}
```

- **`system`** names your system. Use a short lowercase slug: `sap`, `netsuite`, `acme-erp`. `quickbooks` and `xero` are used by EightyOne's own integrations.
- **`externalType`** is the kind of object on your side: `customer`, `item`, `order`, `invoice`. One record can have one id of each type in each system, so a customer and an invoice can both point at the same task.
- **`externalId`** is your id, up to 255 characters, as you send it.
- **`entityType`** is the kind of EightyOne record: `client`, `customer`, `vendor`, `product`, `task`, `work_order`, `purchase_order`, `ssu` (machine) or `storage_unit`.
- **`entityId`** is the record's API id, the same one the rest of the API uses. That's a product's SKU (matched without case), a client's id, a purchase order's number, and the `externalId` of anything else.

## Linking

`PUT /api/v1/external-refs` with the link. Linking is idempotent: sending the same link again only refreshes it (and its `status`, if you send one). Each side maps to one record:

- If your object was linked to another record, it moves to this one.
- If this record already had a different object of that type in your system, that link is replaced.

`status` is optional, up to 32 characters, and kept as given. Use it for documents EightyOne asked your system to create, such as `draft`, `sent` or `paid`.

## Looking up

- **Your id → EightyOne:** `GET /api/v1/external-refs/lookup?system=acme-erp&externalType=item&externalId=ITEM-77`
- **EightyOne → your id:** `GET /api/v1/external-refs/lookup?system=acme-erp&externalType=item&entityType=product&entityId=SKU-1001`

Both answer the link, or `404` when there is none. `GET /api/v1/external-refs` lists links, newest first. Filter it by `system` and `externalType`, or by one record (`entityType` + `entityId`) to see every id it has elsewhere.

## Unlinking

`DELETE /api/v1/external-refs/{system}/{externalType}/{externalId}` removes the link only. Neither the EightyOne record nor your object is changed. Every link and unlink is recorded in the audit log.

## What isn't kept

Ids and statuses only. EightyOne keeps no prices, amounts or totals from any system it is connected to.

---

<!-- https://docs.eightyone.app/guides/accounting.md -->

# Accounting: QuickBooks and Xero

**What it is:** EightyOne connects to a company's accounting system ("the books"). The books stay the place where money lives, and EightyOne never holds a price, a cost or a total. What moves between them is names, ids and quantities:

- **From the books:** customers, vendors and products, and the quantities on hand of tracked items.
- **To the books:** estimates, invoices and purchase orders, as items and quantities. The books price them.

**Providers:** QuickBooks and Xero, with more to come. `accounting.providers` lists them all, with which ones are available. A company connects one at a time.

**Who:** connecting, importing and sending documents need **Manage company settings & integrations**. Seeing the connection and the documents needs **View company settings & integrations**. The stock comparison needs **View inventory**.

## Connecting

1. `accounting.connect` with the provider returns its sign-in page (`authorizationUrl`).
2. A person opens it, signs in to their books and approves.
3. The provider sends them back to EightyOne's **Integrations** page, connected.

An agent can't approve for the company. It can only hand the link to a person. `accounting.test` answers with the books' company name. `accounting.disconnect` erases the stored tokens. Ids already linked are kept, so reconnecting the same books carries on where it left off. Connecting *different* books unlinks the old ids, because they mean nothing in the new books.

## Importing

`accounting.sync` imports `customers`, `vendors` and `products` (all three by default):

- **Customers** become a factory's **customers**, or a managed-services company's **clients**.
- A record already linked to the books is updated (its name, and a product's description and SKU).
- A record with the same name, or a product with the same SKU, is **linked** rather than duplicated.
- Everything else is created and linked. Nothing is deleted because it's gone from the books.
- A new tracked product starts with the books' quantity on hand, in the company's default storage.

The reply counts what was created, linked, updated and skipped, and lists problems: a SKU two items share, a quantity that isn't whole. Every link is an [external ref](integrations.md), so `external_refs.lookup` translates in both directions.

## Documents

| Document | From | Sent when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Estimate | A quote task (task type **is quote**) | The task is done, or someone asks |
| Invoice | A done task, or a shipped shipment (factories) | Someone asks, or the task's type has **Request an invoice when done** |
| Purchase order | A purchase order | It's created |

Asking is `accounting.request_document` with the `kind` and one of `taskId`, `shipmentId` or `purchaseOrderId`. Documents are queued and sent in the background, so completing a task never waits on the books. A failure is retried later: after 1 minute, then 5, 30 and 120, then once more after 12 hours. A refusal that won't change on its own fails at once with the reason, for example a product that isn't linked to an item.

- **One per source:** asking again returns the same document, and asking again for a failed one queues it again. `accounting.retry_document` does the same by id.
- **What goes over:** the customer or vendor, each product as its item in the books, and the quantities. A task's quantities are what was recorded on its form (parts removed or only counted aren't billed). A shipment's are its lines, a PO's are its lines. Each document is marked with EightyOne's reference ("Fix press (task id)", "PO 12: Restock").
- **What comes back:** the document's number, its status in the books, and a link that opens it there. `accounting.list_documents` lists them, by task, shipment, purchase order or status.

If the company's setting **Send invoices and quotes automatically** is on, QuickBooks also emails each new estimate and invoice to the customer.

## Provider differences

| | QuickBooks | Xero |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Customers and vendors | Two separate lists | One list of contacts: a supplier that isn't also a customer is a vendor; every other contact is a customer |
| Documents | Created ready to send | Created as **drafts**: someone approves them in Xero |
| Prices | Read from the item for the one request, never kept | Xero fills them from the item itself |
| Emailing documents | With the company setting | Not from EightyOne: drafts are approved and sent in Xero |
| Test companies | Sandbox companies (the company's sandbox setting) | The Xero demo company, an ordinary organisation |
| Stock adjustments by quantity | Supported by QuickBooks (not used yet) | Not possible: tracked stock only moves through priced documents |

## Stock

The books own the **capitalized inventory**: what the stock is worth. EightyOne owns the **operational inventory**: what is where, by unit, bin, lot and serial. `accounting.inventory_differences` compares, item by item, the books' quantity on hand with EightyOne's stock in the company's own storage. It lists the largest differences first. Nothing is changed on either side: the report is for a person to decide.

## What is never kept

- **No amounts.** Some providers need a price on every line to accept a document. EightyOne reads the item's own price from the books for that one request and never stores, logs or returns it. Error messages from the books are stored with any amount cut out.
- **No passwords.** The connection keeps the provider's refresh token, encrypted, and nothing else.

# Downloads

## The `eightyone` skill

- **Claude Code:** install it as a plugin, which keeps it up to date and connects the MCP server:

  ```
  /plugin marketplace add eightyone-app/eightyone
  /plugin install eightyone@eightyone
  ```

- **Claude apps and other agents:** download [eightyone-skill.zip](../downloads/eightyone-skill.zip) (the latest release) and upload it as a custom skill. Each release is also kept as `eightyone-skill-<version>.zip`.

The skill's version is in its `SKILL.md` (`metadata.version`). It's released with the API, so its tool reference matches the server.

## Machine-readable docs

- [llms.txt](../llms.txt): an index of these docs for agents.
- [llms-full.txt](../llms-full.txt): everything in one file.
- [OpenAPI 3.1](../reference/openapi.json), [factory spec schema](../reference/factory-spec.schema.json).

# EightyOne capabilities

<!-- Generated from src/capabilities/registry.ts by `pnpm docs:api`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every operation EightyOne exposes to code and agents. Each is one capability: the REST API (`/api/v1`, OpenAPI at `/api/v1/openapi.json`) and the MCP server (`/mcp`) are generated from these definitions, so they cannot disagree.

- **MCP:** read capabilities only for now. A capability is either a listed tool or reached through `capabilities_search` / `capabilities_call`; an agent sees only what its credential may run.

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <API key>` (or `X-API-Key`). The key's company is the company; a key acts as its owner, narrowed to the key's permissions.
- **Errors:** RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`.
- **Writes:** send `Idempotency-Key: <unique>` to make a retry safe (24 h). Where marked, `Prefer: dry-run` runs the write, rolls it back and returns the planned changes.

## Account

### `me.get`: Who am I

The caller: the user this credential acts as, the company it is bound to, how it is calling (REST or MCP; human, agent or service account) and the permissions it actually has here (the union of the user's roles' groups ∩ the credential's permissions). Call it first to know what you can do.

**REST:** `GET /api/v1/me` · **Permission:** any member of the company · **Effect:** read · **MCP:** tool `me_get`

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `user` | object | yes |  |
| `company` | object | yes |  |
| `actorType` | `human` \| `agent` \| `service` | yes |  |
| `channel` | string | yes |  |
| `permissions` | string[] | yes |  |

## Guides

### `guide.get`: Read a guide

EightyOne concepts and how to read the data: the glossary, downtime, maintenance, production, inventory, quality, commissioning, what deserves attention, and this company's own guidance (topic "company"). Without a topic, lists the topics. Read the glossary before working on an unfamiliar area.

**REST:** `GET /api/v1/guides` · **Permission:** any member of the company · **Effect:** read · **MCP:** tool `guide_get`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `topic` | `glossary` \| `downtime` \| `maintenance` \| `production` \| `inventory` \| `quality` \| `commissioning` \| `signals` \| `company` |  | "company": what this company's administrators tell agents, including notes on specific machines |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `topic` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `title` | string | yes |  |
| `body` | string | yes | Markdown |
| `topics` | object[] | yes |  |

What the company's administrators tell every AI agent: company-wide guidance and notes on specific machines, work centers, products and task types, with any thresholds they set.

**REST:** `GET /api/v1/guidance` · **Permission:** any member of the company · **Effect:** read · **MCP:** via `capabilities_call`

| `name` | string \| null | yes | What it's about, by name |
| `body` | string | yes |  |
| `thresholds` | object | yes |  |
| `version` | integer | yes |  |
| `reviewedAt` | string (date-time) \| null | yes |  |
| `updatedAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |

Write the guidance agents get for the company, or for one machine, work center, product or task type. Replaces that subject's text; the previous version is kept in the audit log. Every agent connected to the company follows it.

**REST:** `PUT /api/v1/guidance` · **Permission:** `ai_guidance:manage` · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** supported · **MCP:** no

Remove the guidance for the company or one subject. The audit log keeps what it said.

Without the 'See all tasks' permission you see only tasks assigned to you, plus your teams' tasks with 'See tasks for my team'.

### `tasks.update`: Update a task

Change a task, with the dashboard's rules: status changes need 'Change task status from mobile' (assignees may still complete their own work), reassigning needs 'Reassign tasks', blocked tasks can't progress, producing tasks complete with goodQuantity / scrapQuantity (counts during the run: tasks_record_counts), maintenance types may need failure codes (problemCodeId, causeCodeId, remedyCodeId) to complete, 'incomplete' needs a reason and can create a follow-up (createFollowUp), 'declined' needs a reason. Tasks sent to a partner only accept details, dueDate and priorityId.

**REST:** `PATCH /api/v1/tasks/:id` · **Permission:** any member of the company · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** preview (checks the change and lists its effects, without making it) · **MCP:** tool `tasks_update`

### `tasks.record_counts`: Record production counts

Add good and scrap quantities to a running work-order operation or producing task, as operators do from the app. Counts add up and feed OEE; the output posts to stock once, when the task completes. To count at completion instead, pass goodQuantity / scrapQuantity to tasks.update with the status.

**REST:** `POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/counts` · **Permission:** any member of the company · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** supported · **MCP:** tool `tasks_record_counts`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Task external id |
| `goodQuantity` | number |  |  |
| `scrapQuantity` | number |  |  |
| `scrapReasonCodeId` | integer |  | A scrap reason (reason_codes_list, kind scrap) |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes |  |
| `goodQuantity` | number | yes |  |
| `scrapQuantity` | number | yes |  |
| `scrapReasonCodeId` | integer \| null | yes |  |

### `tasks.connect`: Connect two tasks

Link two tasks. 'dependency': the second waits for the first. It can't progress until the first is done, and goes back to open if it was already ready or dispatched (it becomes ready if the first is already done). 'follow': only records that the second follows the first. Connections are removed in the dashboard.

**REST:** `POST /api/v1/tasks/:from/connections` · **Permission:** any member of the company · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** supported · **MCP:** tool `tasks_connect`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string | yes | The first task's external id |
| `to` | string | yes | The external id of the task that waits for or follows it |
| `type` | `dependency` \| `follow` | yes |  |
| `description` | string |  |  |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string | yes |  |
| `to` | string | yes |  |
| `type` | string | yes |  |
| `description` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `toStatus` | string | yes | The second task's status after connecting |

### `tasks.delete`: Delete a task

Delete a task, as the dashboard does: a task you sent to a partner withdraws the handoff; a task a partner sent you can't be deleted (decline it instead).

**REST:** `DELETE /api/v1/tasks/:id` · **Permission:** `tasks:delete` · **Effect:** destructive · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** not supported · **MCP:** no

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes |  |

### `tasks.get_form`: A task's form

The fields a task's form records, in order: type, whether it's required, the choices of a select, the limits of a measurement, whether a condition hides it, and the current answer. Answer them with tasks_submit_form.

**REST:** `GET /api/v1/tasks/:id/form` · **Permission:** any member of the company · **Effect:** read · **MCP:** tool `tasks_get_form`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Task external id |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes |  |
| `fields` | object[] | yes |  |

### `tasks.submit_form`: Fill in a task's form

Answer a task's form fields by title (tasks_get_form lists them), and optionally complete the task (status done or submitted) or mark it incomplete, as the app does. Completing needs every required field; measurements outside their limits open an NCR; machine-status fields set the machine's status. Counts and failure codes go with the completion, as in tasks_update. Preview it first.

**REST:** `POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/form` · **Permission:** any member of the company · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** preview (checks the change and lists its effects, without making it) · **MCP:** tool `tasks_submit_form`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Task external id |
| `answers` | object[] | yes | Answers by field title; fields left out keep their answer |
| `status` | `done` \| `submitted` \| `incomplete` |  | Complete it (done, or submitted for review) or mark it incomplete; leave out to only save the answers |
| `incompleteReason` | string |  |  |
| `createFollowUp` | boolean |  |  |
| `goodQuantity` | number |  |  |
| `scrapQuantity` | number |  |  |
| `scrapReasonCodeId` | integer |  |  |
| `problemCodeId` | integer |  |  |
| `causeCodeId` | integer |  |  |
| `remedyCodeId` | integer |  |  |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Task external id |
| `title` | string | yes |  |
| `details` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `status` | string | yes |  |
| `startDate` | string (date-time) \| null | yes |  |
| `endDate` | string (date-time) \| null | yes |  |
| `dueDate` | string (date-time) \| null | yes |  |
| `priorityId` | integer | yes |  |
| `typeId` | string \| null | yes | Task type external id |
| `team` | object \| null | yes | The team whose members see and take this task: its task type's team (change it on the type) |
| `ssuId` | string \| null | yes | SSU external id |
| `externalSystemId` | string \| null | yes | Your id for the task |
| `incompleteReason` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `declinedReason` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `isPartialCompletion` | boolean | yes | Completed in part; a follow-up task carries the rest |
| `handoffRole` | `proxy` \| `mirror` \| null | yes | proxy: you sent it to a partner; mirror: a partner sent it to you |
| `problemCodeId` | integer \| null | yes | Failure coding: what was wrong |
| `causeCodeId` | integer \| null | yes | Failure coding: why |
| `remedyCodeId` | integer \| null | yes | Failure coding: what fixed it |
| `createdAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `updatedAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `failedChecks` | string[] | yes |  |
| `ncrId` | string \| null | yes |  |

## Task types

### `task_types.list`: List task types

The company's task types: the templates every task is created from (work orders' operations, maintenance, NCRs, inspections, approvals…), alphabetically. Use a type's `id` as `typeId` when creating a task.

**REST:** `GET /api/v1/task-types` · **Permission:** any member of the company · **Effect:** read · **MCP:** tool `task_types_list`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer |  | Page size (1–100, default 50) |
| `offset` | integer |  | Rows to skip |

**Output:** `{ data, pagination }`, each item:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Task type external id |
| `typeName` | string | yes |  |
| `color` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `isQuote` | boolean | yes | A done task sends its products and quantities as an estimate to the connected books |
| `requestInvoiceOnDone` | boolean | yes | A done task sends an invoice request to the connected books |
| `isUserGenerated` | boolean | yes | Field users may create tasks of this type themselves |
| `isDataRequest` | boolean | yes | Tasks of this type ask a partner company for traceability data |
| `isRemote` | boolean | yes |  |
| `isInventory` | boolean | yes |  |
| `defaultUseTransit` | boolean | yes | Inventory tasks stage stock through the transit bin by default |
| `isBulk` | boolean | yes |  |
| `workCenterId` | integer \| null | yes |  |
| `team` | object \| null | yes | The team whose members see and take this type's tasks. Changing it moves every task of the type |
| `parentProductId` | integer \| null | yes | The product a production operation of this type makes |
| `createdAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `updatedAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |

## Teams

### `teams.list`: List teams

The company's teams, alphabetically, with their members' personnel ids. A task belongs to its task type's team: team members with 'See tasks for my team' see those tasks and can take them in the field.

**REST:** `GET /api/v1/teams` · **Permission:** any member of the company · **Effect:** read · **MCP:** via `capabilities_call`

**Output:** `{ data, pagination }`, each item:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Team id |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `color` | string | yes |  |
| `memberIds` | integer[] | yes | Personnel ids of the members |
| `createdAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `updatedAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |

### `teams.create`: Create a team

Create a team, optionally with its members. Point task types at it to give it work.

**REST:** `POST /api/v1/teams` · **Permission:** `settings:manage` · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** supported · **MCP:** no

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `color` | string |  | Hex color, e.g. #026485 |
| `memberIds` | integer[] |  | Personnel ids: replaces the members |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Team id |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `color` | string | yes |  |

| `createdAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `updatedAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |

### `teams.update`: Update a team

Rename or recolor a team, or replace its members (memberIds). Only the fields sent change. Members see the team's tasks at once.

**REST:** `PATCH /api/v1/teams/:id` · **Permission:** `settings:manage` · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** supported · **MCP:** no

| `updatedAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |

### `teams.delete`: Delete a team

Delete a team and its memberships. Refused while a task type still belongs to it: move those types to another team (or none) first.

### `inventory.stock_levels`: Stock on hand

Goods on hand per product and storage site (up to 2000 rows), by the same rule reordering uses: good stock only (not the bads bin), not counting stock held by a partner. Filter by product id, SKU or storage site.

**REST:** `GET /api/v1/inventory/stock-levels` · **Permission:** `inventory:view` · **Effect:** read · **MCP:** tool `inventory_stock_levels`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `productId` | string |  | Product external id |
| `sku` | string |  | Product SKU (case-insensitive) |
| `storageSiteId` | string |  | Storage site external id |

**Output:** `{ data, pagination }`, each item:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

### `stock.transfer`: Move stock

**REST:** `POST /api/v1/stock/transfers` · **Permission:** `inventory:manage` · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** preview (checks the change and lists its effects, without making it) · **MCP:** tool `stock_transfer`

| `to` | string | yes | Storage unit external id it goes to |

| `toBin` | `goods` \| `bads` \| `quarantine` |  | The bin it lands in (default: the same) |
| `lotCode` | string |  | Which lot, for lot-tracked products |
| `serialCode` | string |  | Which unit, for serialized products |

### `shipments.ship`: Ship it

Confirm a draft shipment left: each line's goods come out of stock, written to the customer. For a customer that is an EightyOne company, the goods arrive in their transit. Refused if any line lacks the stock, names a lot that isn't available, or takes another customer's consigned stock. Needs 'Manage inventory'. Preview it first.

**REST:** `POST /api/v1/shipments/:id/ship` · **Permission:** `inventory:manage` · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** preview (checks the change and lists its effects, without making it) · **MCP:** tool `shipments_ship`

### `inventory_counts.finalize`: Finish a cycle count

Close counting: each line's expected quantity becomes what's on hand now, discrepancies are computed, and anything on hand the count never saw becomes a line counted 0. Nothing is posted to stock until it's reconciled. Needs 'Manage inventory'.

**REST:** `POST /api/v1/inventory-counts/:id/finalize` · **Permission:** `inventory:manage` · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** supported · **MCP:** tool `inventory_counts_finalize`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | yes |  |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | yes |  |
| `storageUnit` | object \| null | yes |  |
| `status` | string | yes | draft / in_progress / completed (finalized, awaiting reconciliation) / reconciled |
| `countType` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `totalExpected` | number \| null | yes |  |
| `totalCounted` | number \| null | yes |  |
| `taskId` | string \| null | yes | The count task operators fill in, if any |
| `dueDate` | string (date-time) \| null | yes |  |
| `completedAt` | string (date-time) \| null | yes |  |
| `reconciledAt` | string (date-time) \| null | yes |  |
| `createdAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `lines` | object[] | yes |  |

### `inventory_counts.reconcile`: Post a cycle count to stock

Decide each line of a finalized count and post it. accepted: stock becomes the counted quantity; adjusted: becomes adjustedQuantity; ignored (and any line not listed): stock stays as the system has it. Every write-off needs an adjustment reasonCodeId (reason_codes_list kind adjustment). Needs 'Manage inventory' and 'Adjust inventory'. Preview it first: it lists each addition, write-off and bin move.

**REST:** `POST /api/v1/inventory-counts/:id/reconcile` · **Permission:** `inventory:manage` + `inventory:adjust` · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** preview (checks the change and lists its effects, without making it) · **MCP:** tool `inventory_counts_reconcile`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | yes |  |
| `decisions` | object[] | yes |  |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | yes |  |
| `storageUnit` | object \| null | yes |  |
| `status` | string | yes | draft / in_progress / completed (finalized, awaiting reconciliation) / reconciled |
| `countType` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `totalExpected` | number \| null | yes |  |
| `totalCounted` | number \| null | yes |  |
| `taskId` | string \| null | yes | The count task operators fill in, if any |
| `dueDate` | string (date-time) \| null | yes |  |
| `completedAt` | string (date-time) \| null | yes |  |
| `reconciledAt` | string (date-time) \| null | yes |  |
| `createdAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `lines` | object[] | yes |  |

| `createdAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `updatedAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |

### `work_orders.upsert`: Create or update a work order (ERP orders in)

Idempotent on externalSystemId: a new id creates a draft order; re-sending updates it while it is still a draft and is a no-op afterwards. Lands on the product's released routing when there is exactly one. Release it with work_orders.release.

**REST:** `POST /api/v1/work-orders` · **Permission:** `production:manage` · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** supported · **MCP:** no

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `externalSystemId` | string | yes | Your (ERP) id for the order: the upsert key |
| `productId` | integer |  | EightyOne product id (or give productSku) |
| `productSku` | string |  | Product SKU (case-insensitive) |
| `quantity` | number |  |  |
| `uom` | string |  |  |
| `dueDate` | string (date-time) \| string (date) |  |  |
| `code` | string |  | Human code; defaults to the next WO-n |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workOrder` | object | yes |  |
| `created` | boolean | yes |  |

### `work_orders.batch_upsert`: Create or update many work orders

Upsert up to 500 orders; each succeeds or fails on its own (results in input order).

**REST:** `POST /api/v1/work-orders/batch` · **Permission:** `production:manage` · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** supported · **MCP:** no

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orders` | any[] | yes | Each item is a work_orders.upsert input; an invalid item fails on its own |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `results` | object[] | yes |  |

### `webhooks.create`: Create a webhook

Subscribe a URL to events. Deliveries are Standard Webhooks messages signed with EightyOne's Ed25519 key: verify them with the public keys at /api/v1/webhook-signing-keys. There is no secret to store.

**REST:** `POST /api/v1/webhooks` · **Permission:** `webhooks:manage` · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** not supported · **MCP:** no

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `targetUrl` | string (uri) | yes | HTTPS endpoint; private and internal addresses are refused |
| `eventTypes` | `task.status_changed` \| `task.created` \| `client.created` \| `work_order.released` \| `work_order.completed` \| `downtime.started` \| `downtime.ended` \| `lot.created` \| `stock.reorder_triggered` \| `handoff.received` \| `handoff.status_changed` \| `handoff.declined` \| `handoff.deleted` \| `partner_delivery.incoming` \| `partner_delivery.received` \| `partner_delivery.shortfall` \| `data_package.received`[] | yes |  |
| `headers` | object |  | Extra headers sent with each delivery |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes |  |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `targetUrl` | string | yes |  |
| `eventTypes` | string[] | yes |  |
| `isActive` | boolean | yes |  |
| `failureCount` | integer | yes |  |
| `disabledAt` | string (date-time) \| null | yes | Set when repeated failures switched the webhook off |
| `headers` | object \| null | yes |  |
| `createdAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `updatedAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `verification` | object | yes | Verify each delivery's signature with EightyOne's public key |

## Partner network

### `handoffs.send`: Send a task to a partner company

Hand one of your tasks to another EightyOne company (by its short name, or a partner subcontractor). The partner gets its own copy; your people come off the task. Goods can travel with it (items), and a data-request task carries the scopes it asks for.

**REST:** `POST /api/v1/handoffs` · **Permission:** `handoffs:send` · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** supported · **MCP:** tool `handoffs_send`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `taskId` | string | yes | Your task's id |
| `recipientShortName` | string |  |  |
| `subContractorId` | integer |  | A subcontractor that is an EightyOne company |
| `items` | object[] |  |  |
| `dataRequest` | object |  |  |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes |  |
| `direction` | `incoming` \| `outgoing` | yes |  |
| `state` | string | yes |  |
| `partner` | object | yes |  |
| `taskId` | string | yes | This company's own task (never the partner's) |
| `status` | string | yes |  |
| `declinedReason` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `requestedItems` | object[] | yes |  |
| `dataRequest` | object \| null | yes |  |
| `deliveries` | object[] | yes |  |
| `linkActive` | boolean | yes |  |
| `createdAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |

## Analytics

### `analytics.overview`: Factory performance overview

Headline numbers for a window: total downtime, failures, average availability and OEE, and how many machines are monitored. `unavailableMetrics` names OEE factors with no source data yet. Start here, then drill into analytics.downtime / analytics.reliability.

**REST:** `GET /api/v1/analytics/overview` · **Permission:** `insights:view` · **Effect:** read · **MCP:** tool `analytics_overview`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string (date-time) \| string (date) |  | Window start (ISO 8601). Default: 30 days before `to` |
| `to` | string (date-time) \| string (date) |  | Window end, exclusive (ISO 8601). Default: now |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `range` | object | yes |  |
| `downtimeSeconds` | number | yes |  |
| `downtimeHours` | number | yes |  |
| `failures` | integer | yes |  |
| `avgAvailability` | number \| null | yes | 0–1 |
| `avgOee` | number \| null | yes | 0–1 |
| `monitoredSsus` | integer | yes |  |
| `unavailableMetrics` | string[] | yes |  |

### `analytics.downtime`: Downtime by machine

Time each machine (SSU) spent DOWN or in MAINTENANCE in the window, most first, with how many times it entered that state. For the reasons, follow up with downtime_events.list (reason-coded stoppages) or storylines.ssu (the machine's story).

**REST:** `GET /api/v1/analytics/downtime` · **Permission:** `insights:view` · **Effect:** read · **MCP:** tool `analytics_downtime`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string (date-time) \| string (date) |  | Window start (ISO 8601). Default: 30 days before `to` |
| `to` | string (date-time) \| string (date) |  | Window end, exclusive (ISO 8601). Default: now |

**Output:** `{ data, pagination }`, each item:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ssuId` | string \| null | yes | SSU external id |
| `ssuName` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `category` | string | yes | DOWN or MAINTENANCE |
| `seconds` | number | yes |  |
| `hours` | number | yes |  |
| `transitions` | integer | yes | Times the machine entered this state |

### `analytics.reliability`: Machine reliability (MTTR / MTBF)

Per machine: failures (entries into DOWN), mean time to repair and mean time between failures, in seconds, most failures first.

**REST:** `GET /api/v1/analytics/reliability` · **Permission:** `insights:view` · **Effect:** read · **MCP:** tool `analytics_reliability`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string (date-time) \| string (date) |  | Window start (ISO 8601). Default: 30 days before `to` |
| `to` | string (date-time) \| string (date) |  | Window end, exclusive (ISO 8601). Default: now |

| `mtbfSeconds` | number \| null | yes |  |

## Machines

### `downtime_events.list`: List machine stoppages

Individual downtime events (newest first, up to 500): when each machine stopped, for how long, and the reason code someone classified it with. Use it to explain the totals from analytics.downtime. Filter by machine and window; `unclassifiedOnly` lists stops still waiting for a reason.

**REST:** `GET /api/v1/downtime-events` · **Permission:** any member of the company · **Effect:** read · **MCP:** tool `downtime_events_list`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ssuId` | string |  | SSU external id |
| `from` | string (date-time) \| string (date) |  | Stops that started at or after this time |
| `to` | string (date-time) \| string (date) |  | Stops that started before this time |
| `unclassifiedOnly` | boolean \| `true` \| `false` |  |  |
| `openOnly` | boolean \| `true` \| `false` |  | Only machines still stopped |

**Output:** `{ data, pagination }`, each item:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | yes |  |
| `ssuId` | string | yes | SSU external id |
| `ssuName` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `startedAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `endedAt` | string (date-time) \| null | yes | null while the machine is still stopped |
| `durationSeconds` | number \| null | yes |  |
| `source` | `auto` \| `manual` | yes | auto: detected from machine telemetry; manual: reported by a person |
| `reason` | object \| null | yes | The downtime reason code, once someone classified the stop |
| `note` | string \| null | yes |  |

### `downtime_events.summary`: Downtime by machine and reason

Recorded stoppages per machine in a window (default: the last 30 days), most stopped time first, each broken down by reason code: the direct answer to "which machines were down most, and why?". Counts only the part of each stop inside the window; a stop still open counts up to the window end. Complements analytics.downtime, which measures time in a DOWN / MAINTENANCE status.

**REST:** `GET /api/v1/downtime-events/summary` · **Permission:** any member of the company · **Effect:** read · **MCP:** tool `downtime_events_summary`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string (date-time) \| string (date) |  | Window start (ISO 8601). Default: 30 days before `to` |
| `to` | string (date-time) \| string (date) |  | Window end, exclusive (ISO 8601). Default: now |

**Output:** `{ data, pagination }`, each item:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ssuId` | string | yes | SSU external id |
| `ssuName` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `seconds` | number | yes |  |
| `hours` | number | yes |  |
| `stops` | integer | yes |  |
| `openStops` | integer | yes | Stops not yet ended |
| `byReason` | object[] | yes |  |

## Quality

### `ncrs.open`: Open an NCR

Open a nonconformance report: a task of the company's NCR task type (Settings), linked to the task it was found on and carrying its machine and work order, with the affected lot or product recorded on it. A failed in-line check opens one by itself; use this for what people find. Disposition it with ncrs_disposition.

**REST:** `POST /api/v1/ncrs` · **Permission:** any member of the company · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** preview (checks the change and lists its effects, without making it) · **MCP:** tool `ncrs_open`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | yes | What's wrong, in a line |
| `details` | string |  | What was found: measurements, quantities, how it was noticed |
| `foundOn` | string |  | External id of the task it was found on (an operation or inspection): the NCR takes its machine and work order |
| `ssuId` | string |  | SSU external id, when not taken from foundOn |
| `workOrderId` | string |  | Work order external id, when not taken from foundOn |
| `lotCode` | string |  | The affected lot |
| `productSku` | string |  | The affected product |
| `priorityId` | integer |  |  |
| `assigneeIds` | integer[] |  | Personnel ids |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Task external id |
| `title` | string | yes |  |
| `details` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `status` | string | yes |  |
| `startDate` | string (date-time) \| null | yes |  |
| `endDate` | string (date-time) \| null | yes |  |
| `dueDate` | string (date-time) \| null | yes |  |
| `priorityId` | integer | yes |  |
| `typeId` | string \| null | yes | Task type external id |
| `team` | object \| null | yes | The team whose members see and take this task: its task type's team (change it on the type) |
| `ssuId` | string \| null | yes | SSU external id |
| `externalSystemId` | string \| null | yes | Your id for the task |
| `incompleteReason` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `declinedReason` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `isPartialCompletion` | boolean | yes | Completed in part; a follow-up task carries the rest |
| `handoffRole` | `proxy` \| `mirror` \| null | yes | proxy: you sent it to a partner; mirror: a partner sent it to you |
| `problemCodeId` | integer \| null | yes | Failure coding: what was wrong |
| `causeCodeId` | integer \| null | yes | Failure coding: why |
| `remedyCodeId` | integer \| null | yes | Failure coding: what fixed it |
| `createdAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `updatedAt` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `foundOn` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `lotCode` | string \| null | yes |  |
| `productSku` | string \| null | yes |  |

### `ncrs.disposition`: Disposition an NCR

Decide what happens to nonconforming material, once per NCR. use_as_is: recorded only. rework: creates a rework task (of reworkTaskTypeId, or the NCR's own type). scrap: moves `quantity` of the lot to the bads bin and blocks the lot. return: blocks the lot for return to the vendor. Needs 'Disposition NCRs'.

**REST:** `POST /api/v1/ncrs/:id/disposition` · **Permission:** `ncr:disposition` · **Effect:** write · **Idempotency-Key:** accepted · **Dry run:** supported · **MCP:** tool `ncrs_disposition`

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | The NCR's task external id |
| `disposition` | `use_as_is` \| `rework` \| `scrap` \| `return` | yes |  |
| `lotCode` | string |  | The affected lot (scrap and return act on it) |
| `quantity` | number |  | For scrap: how much of the lot |
| `reworkTaskTypeId` | string |  | For rework: the task type's external id |
| `notes` | string |  |  |

**Output**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes |  |
| `disposition` | `use_as_is` \| `rework` \| `scrap` \| `return` | yes |  |
| `lot` | object \| null | yes |  |
| `reworkTaskId` | string \| null | yes | The rework task's external id |

## Storylines

| `chapters` | object[] | yes |  |
